source.title: ESCAPE: An Open-Label Trial of Personalized Immunotherapy in Critically Ill COVID-19 Patients
source.source_type: exploratory phase II multicenter open-label prospective clinical trial

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary trial design, central efficacy and safety results, key immune/biomarker findings, major subgroup findings, explicit limitations, and disclosures were atomized. Bibliographic entries and every baseline-table cell were not atomized.

atoms.canonical_statement: ESCAPE evaluated whether biomarker-guided personalized immunotherapy was associated with clinical improvement in critically ill adults with SARS-CoV-2 ARDS.
ESCAPE was an exploratory phase II, open-label, prospective trial conducted in 4 internal-medicine departments and 7 intensive care units at Greek tertiary hospitals between April and November 2020.
Eligible patients were adults with ARDS from SARS-CoV-2 and laboratory evidence of macrophage activation-like syndrome (MALS) or complex immune dysregulation (CID).

population.label: Adults with SARS-CoV-2 ARDS and MALS or CID

atoms.canonical_statement: MALS was defined as any serum ferritin concentration greater than 4,420 ng/mL.
CID was defined as ferritin at or below 4,420 ng/mL plus low HLA-DR expression on CD14 monocytes: fewer than 5,000 membrane receptors or 30 mean-fluorescence-intensity units.
Supplementary enrollment criteria required radiographic lower-respiratory-tract infiltrates, at least two respiratory symptoms/signs, and at least two physiologic or laboratory severity criteria.

population.label: Lower respiratory tract involvement criteria
inclusion_criteria: compatible infiltrates on chest radiograph or CT
at least 2 of new/worsening cough, dyspnea, compatible rales
at least 2 of PCT ≥0.25 ng/mL, PaO2 ≤60 mmHg or room-air oxygen saturation ≤90%, respiratory rate ≥20/min

atoms.canonical_statement: Exclusions included stage IV malignancy, a do-not-resuscitate decision, active tuberculosis, HIV infection, primary immunodeficiency, corticosteroid use longer than 15 days, recent anti-cytokine biologic treatment, systemic lupus erythematosus, demyelinating disease, pregnancy, or lactation.

population.label: ESCAPE eligibility exclusions
exclusion_criteria: anti-cytokine biologic treatment in previous month

atoms.canonical_statement: Of 144 patients screened, 102 were enrolled in the intention-to-treat population after 42 exclusions.
Sixty patients received anakinra; 14 had MALS and 46 had CID with hematologic or liver dysfunction that made tocilizumab unsuitable.
Forty-two patients with CID and a hematologic/liver profile permitting tocilizumab received tocilizumab.
Anakinra was administered intravenously at 200 mg every 8 hours for 7 days to patients assigned to anakinra by immune phenotype and treatment-eligibility criteria.
For creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min, the anakinra regimen was reduced to 100 mg intravenously every 8 hours for 7 days.
Tocilizumab was administered intravenously as a single 8 mg/kg dose, capped at 800 mg.
The primary endpoint was a composite of at least a 25% decrease in baseline SOFA score and/or at least a 50% increase in baseline PaO2/FiO2 by day 8.

outcome.definition: ≥25% decrease in baseline SOFA and/or ≥50% increase in baseline PaO2/FiO2

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary endpoints were 28-day mortality, change in SOFA score by day 28, serum biomarker changes, and changes in cytokine production by peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

outcome.definition: 28-day mortality; day-28 SOFA change; serum biomarkers; PBMC cytokine production

atoms.canonical_statement: Exploratory endpoints were the WHO clinical progression scale and length of hospital stay.

concept.text: WHO clinical progression scale and hospital length of stay

atoms.canonical_statement: A concurrent no-immunotherapy comparison cohort of 84 patients was selected from 136 admissions at three other Greek ICUs using ESCAPE inclusion and exclusion criteria except that the laboratory CID criterion was unavailable and was not applied.

exposures.details: Selected contemporaneously; CID laboratory screening unavailable

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary endpoint was compared with Fisher exact testing and forward stepwise logistic regression; serial biomarkers used paired Wilcoxon tests, cytokine correlations used Spearman rank correlation, WHO scale distributions used Pearson chi-square testing, and discharge time used a log-rank test.
The trial was explicitly exploratory and no a priori power calculation was performed.
The supplement describes quantitative HLA-DR flow cytometry on CD14/CD45 monocytes and ex vivo PBMC stimulation with LPS or heat-killed Candida albicans followed by cytokine measurement.

Adverse events and serious adverse events were collected from baseline through the last evaluation, with investigators instructed to record all events and assess seriousness and relationship to study drug.
The day-8 primary composite endpoint occurred in 35/60 anakinra-treated patients (58.3%) and 14/42 tocilizumab-treated patients (33.3%), OR 2.80 (95% CI 1.23-6.37; p=0.02).
In forward stepwise logistic regression, anakinra treatment remained associated with meeting the primary endpoint, adjusted OR 3.11 (95% CI 1.29-7.73; p=0.01).

adjustment_variables: Charlson Comorbidity Index and variables entered into forward stepwise model

atoms.canonical_statement: A ≥25% decrease in SOFA by day 8 occurred in 23/60 anakinra patients (38.3%) and 7/42 tocilizumab patients (16.7%), OR 3.11 (95% CI 1.19-8.15; p=0.03).
A ≥50% increase in PaO2/FiO2 by day 8 occurred in 18/60 anakinra patients (30.0%) and 12/42 tocilizumab patients (28.6%), OR 1.07 (95% CI 0.45-2.55; p=1.00).
Twenty-eight-day mortality was 20/60 (33.3%) with anakinra and 14/42 (33.3%) with tocilizumab, OR 1.00 (95% CI 0.43-2.31; p=1.00).
Median day-28 SOFA change did not differ significantly between anakinra (-10.0; Q1-Q3 -75 to 257) and tocilizumab (0; -55 to 440), p=0.32.

By day 28, the WHO clinical progression-scale distribution was shifted toward lower severity among anakinra-treated survivors compared with concurrent comparators (p=0.011) and tocilizumab-treated patients (p=0.008).
Median time to hospital discharge was 20 days with anakinra and 31 days with tocilizumab; the discharge curves differed by log-rank testing (p=0.012).
Among patients with MALS, 28-day mortality was 9/14 (64.3%) in anakinra-treated ESCAPE patients and 6/7 (85.7%) in concurrent comparators; the article reports p=0.03 by binomial test.

population.label: MALS subgroup: anakinra-treated ESCAPE patients plus concurrent comparators

atoms.canonical_statement: Absolute lymphocyte count increased from day 1 to day 8 with anakinra (p=0.003) but not with tocilizumab (p=0.506).
PaO2/FiO2 increased from day 1 to day 8 with anakinra (p<0.0001), whereas the tocilizumab within-group comparison was not significant (p=0.077).
Serum ferritin decreased from day 1 to day 4 with anakinra (p=0.001) but not with tocilizumab (p=0.589).
Serum IL-6 increased from day 1 to day 4 with tocilizumab (p=0.005), while the anakinra comparison was not significant (p=0.222).
Serum suPAR increased from day 1 to day 4 with tocilizumab (p=0.003), while the anakinra comparison was not significant (p=0.126).
Absolute HLA-DR molecules on circulating monocytes increased after tocilizumab (p=0.001) but did not significantly change after anakinra (p=0.627).
HLA-DR mean fluorescence intensity increased after tocilizumab (p<0.0001); the anakinra within-group comparison also reached p=0.046 but in the opposite direction shown in the figure.
Ex vivo LPS-stimulated PBMC IL-6 production increased by day 4 in the anakinra group (p=0.049), while the tocilizumab comparison was not significant (p=0.345).
Ex vivo heat-killed Candida-stimulated PBMC IL-6 production increased by day 4 in the anakinra group (p=0.017), while the tocilizumab comparison was not significant (p=0.494).
Among anakinra-treated patients, day-4 Candida-stimulated PBMC IL-6 production correlated inversely with day-28 WHO clinical progression scale, Spearman rs=-0.488 (p=0.004).

population.label: Anakinra-treated patients with paired PBMC/clinical data

atoms.canonical_statement: Ventilator-associated pneumonia occurred in 9/60 anakinra patients (15.0%) and 15/42 tocilizumab patients (35.7%), p=0.02.

atoms.canonical_statement: Bloodstream infection occurred in 13/60 anakinra patients (21.7%) and 17/42 tocilizumab patients (40.5%), p=0.049.

atoms.canonical_statement: Within anakinra-treated patients, the primary endpoint occurred in 6/14 MALS patients (42.9%) and 29/46 CID patients with hematologic/liver dysfunction (63.0%), OR 0.440 (95% CI 0.130-1.483; p=0.223).

exposures.details: MALS and CID subgroup comparison within anakinra-treated patients

quantitative_result.effect_measure: odds ratio for MALS versus CID

atoms.canonical_statement: Within anakinra-treated patients, 28-day mortality was 9/14 for MALS (64.3%) and 11/46 for CID with hematologic/liver dysfunction (23.9%), OR 5.727 (95% CI 1.583-20.725; p=0.009).

atoms.canonical_statement: Within anakinra-treated patients, median percent delta SOFA at day 28 was 200% (Q1-Q3 -3 to 440) in MALS versus -33.3% (-75 to 83) in CID with hematologic/liver dysfunction (p=0.019).

The authors concluded that immune assessment identified critically ill COVID-19 patients with MALS or related immune dysregulation who appeared to have favorable responses to biomarker-guided anakinra treatment.

The authors stated that the apparent primary-endpoint advantage of anakinra over tocilizumab should not be interpreted as direct drug superiority because the immune-classification and treatment-assignment scheme probably favored anakinra.
The study lacked a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy design.
The concurrent comparator cohort lacked CID immune assessment, so it could not reproduce the trial’s immune-endotype selection process.
Coadministration rates of azithromycin, hydroxychloroquine, remdesivir, and dexamethasone differed between the treated trial population and concurrent comparators.
Several baseline features differed between the phenotype-assigned anakinra and tocilizumab groups, including hypertension, AST, ALT, glycopeptide use, and moxifloxacin use.
The authors called for confirmation of the biomarker-guided anakinra strategy in a randomized clinical trial.

The study was funded by the Hellenic Institute for the Study of Sepsis and the Horizon 2020 RISKinCOVID grant (grant agreement 961844); the authors state that funders had no role in design, analysis, interpretation, or manuscript preparation.
Several authors reported advisory, grant, honoraria, founder, or patent-related relationships, while other authors declared no conflicts; the article provides author-level disclosures.
Online supplementary material associated with the article was made available with the online version.
